text:
priya: Quick heads-up — we need to finalize the region mix for Q3 commitments for the inference fleet. I pulled a billing export and some of the effective costs are surprising. High level: US-W and EU-W are pretty close once we factor committed discounts; APAC is still a 30–40% premium. Also seeing non-trivial egress when models and data cross regions. Can we surface tradeoffs here?

alex: Pushed a quick cost delta I ran against last 90 days. Raw per-GPU-hour (pX-like) I pulled from pricing API:
- us-west: $3.20/hr
- eu-west: $3.60/hr
- ap-southeast: $4.50/hr
Committed 1yr typical discounts we see: us-west ~30%, eu-west ~28%, apac ~20% -> effective per-GPU-hour: us-west $2.24, eu-west $2.59, apac $3.60.
Also note minimum commitment term and regional SKUs differ (apac lacks newer dense GPU SKU so perf/cost differs).

lucy: Important to add latency constraints: for EU customers serving from us-west adds ~70–120ms P50 for our chat endpoints and ~40–60ms for embeddings. For real-time features that matters. APAC latency from US is >200ms which is borderline for interactive UIs.

jon: billing-bot uploaded a short sheet: https://billing.internal/redwood/q3-region-costs (useful pivot table + per-customer egress). Also flagged a recurring cross-region replication job that moves ~200TB/mo between EU and US — that explains a chunk of egress line items.

priya: TL;DR tradeoffs to consider: cost delta vs latency vs available committed SKU capacity. Proposed quick starting mix for 1yr commit: 60% us-west reserved, 30% eu-west reserved, 10% apac on-demand/spot for burst. That keeps committed capacity where price is best but reserves some EU capacity for lower-latency EU traffic and leaves APAC flexible. Thoughts?

mia: Two more constraints: 1) APAC availability zones for our preferred GPU SKU are small — autoscaler cold-starts are longer; 2) cross-region egress EU->US currently billed ~ $0.08/GB in our cloud contract. At 1PB/mo that’s ~ $80k/mo — so colocating models with primary data reduces egress line dramatically.

alex: Agreed on egress. I can run a quick 30-day simulation using recent traffic patterns to estimate commit utilization and effective $/generated-token by region. Running command:
```
python infra/tools/sim_commit.py --regions us-west=0.6,eu-west=0.3,apac=0.1 --horizon_days 90 --traffic_csv gs://billing-prod/traffic/last_90_days.csv
```
I'll share the CSV outputs + cost/latency breakdown. If we assume the replication job stays, eu-west benefits more because it avoids the EU->US replication egress for EU-origin traffic.

jon: I'll add filters to billing export to separate storage replication egress vs request egress; that will let us attribute costs to placement decisions. Also will check if any cross-region interconnect discounts apply for our accounts.

lucy: If alex's sim shows <5% total cost delta between the mixed commit and a US-heavy commit, we should prefer EU placement for EU traffic to preserve latency SLOs. For APAC, prefer on-demand + more aggressive cache + KV prefix caching to reduce token cost until we get better reserved pricing or local SKUs.

priya: Action items: 1) alex -> run sim and post numbers (EOD Thu), 2) lucy -> validate latency impact on embedding endpoints with perf test (by Fri), 3) jon -> separate egress types in billing and check interconnect discounts (Thu), 4) mia -> inventory of APAC SKU availability and expected autoscaler cold-start delta. If sim shows committed placement increases overall cost by <5% but improves latency for region users, we prefer regional placement. :thumbsup:

alex: :eyes: starting sim now, will ping with results.

lucy: noted, will schedule perf run this afternoon.

jon: adding the egress split filters now — will attach a breakdown to the thread when ready.

mia: copying infra-sre on the APAC capacity constraint so they can advise on warm pool sizing.

priya: Great — thanks all. We'll reconvene here once sims + billing split are in.
